Video Editing Skill Pack

41 skills that turn a to-camera recording into a polished motion video with Claude Code. One build, every platform. Every frame is code.

--- I edit my videos with Claude Code now. No CapCut, no Premiere, no editor. Claude cuts the take, builds every motion graphic as code in your brand, draws each frame and renders the MP4. One build gives you a 9:16 reel, a 4:5 LinkedIn video, a 1:1 ad and a 16:9 video for YouTube, your website or a sales email. These skills are the steps I use, with the rules that came out of real drafts I threw away. On top of them sit 20 one-command effects that run on your own clip. ## Install ```bash npx skills add charlie947/reel-editing-skills -g ``` Then open Claude Code in an empty folder and run `video-intake` with your recording. Run `brand-setup` once with your website. You need `ffmpeg`, Node 18 or newer and Python 3. Whisper (free, local) gives the word timings. `behind-my-head`, `tier-list` and the 20 effects also cut you out of the frame with RobustVideoMatting (free, local, `python3 -m pip install torch torchvision`). The model downloads once and is GPL-3.0 licensed.
Manual copy ```bash git clone https://github.com/charlie947/reel-editing-skills.git mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills cp -R reel-editing-skills/skills/* ~/.claude/skills/ ```
## What you can make | You need | Run | |---|---| | A demo of your product or website | `product-demo` | | How it works, a process or a framework | `explainer-video` | | A founder take or an opinion piece | `big-idea-video` | | A ranking, best to worst | `tier-list` | | Commentary on news in your industry | `news-reaction` | | A feature list, a service menu or a roundup | `toolkit-video` | | Results, a case study or this quarter's numbers | `animated-numbers` inside any of the above | | The best moments from a call, webinar, podcast or long video | `call-clips` | ## How it works Every edit is one HTML page with a `seek(t)` function. It draws any moment of the video from the time alone. A small script shoots every frame in Chrome and ffmpeg turns them into an H.264 file no platform washes out. `video-intake` sets up that page for you (the starter lives inside the skill). Every other skill edits one file in it, `video.js`. ``` your recording → video-intake → brand-setup → opening-hook → a video type → moves → video-sound → video-check → every-format ``` ## The skills ### Start | Skill | What it does | |---|---| | `video-intake` | Checks the file, transcribes word by word, cuts pauses on true silence, sets up the project | | `brand-setup` | Reads your website's real styles. Your colours, font and logo go into every video | | `opening-hook` | The two lines on screen from frame 0, in three tested looks. They double as the thumbnail | ### Video types (pick one per video, or mix by beat) | Skill | What it makes | |---|---| | `product-demo` | Your real site or app on screen. One exact highlight lands on each feature as you name it | | `explainer-video` | Clean canvas, one object per point that changes on the word. My best motion video | | `big-idea-video` | One big 3D object per beat that acts out the idea you say | | `news-reaction` | Industry news over real footage, one clean run per spoken line | | `toolkit-video` | A prompt bar types each item and shows what it does, every 2 seconds | | `call-clips` | A long recording you already have into the 3 to 5 best short clips, ranked, with hooks and captions | | `tier-list` | An S to F tier list. Each item drops into its row on the word, your head breaks out of the card below | ### Moves | Skill | What it does | |---|---| | `zoom-cut` | Zooms into the thing you point at instead of a hard cut | | `word-highlight` | One box exactly on a word or a number, measured off the pixels | | `animated-numbers` | Counts, flip clocks and rings that land on the spoken number | | `behind-my-head` | Cuts you out and puts a real page or a big number behind you, landing on the word | | `call-to-action` | The right ending for each place: comment keyword, links in the post, or a book-a-call card | ### Looks | Skill | What it does | |---|---| | `apple-style` | Light canvas, glass, springs | | `stripe-style` | Fintech look, fast snap ease, 16 ready payment moments | ### Finish | Skill | What it does | |---|---| | `video-sound` | Voice at one gain, music 12 dB under to the last frame, the right loudness per platform | | `video-check` | File format, safe zones, reading time, loudness and a contact sheet to look at | | `every-format` | One build, four sizes: 9:16, 4:5, 1:1 and 16:9, each with that platform's rules | ### Effects (one command on your own clip) Each effect is its own skill and runs on the shared engine in `video-effects`. Set that up once (`npm i puppeteer` in its folder), then: ```bash node ~/.claude/skills/video-effects/run.cjs grid-dive my-clip.mp4 grid-dive.mp4 ``` | Skill | What it does to your clip | |---|---| | `video-effects` | The shared engine. Fits your clip, cuts you out, renders the MP4 | | `grid-dive` | Pulls back into a wall of tiles of your clip, then dives back in | | `title-orbit` | Your words circle your head, then the camera flies through a letter | | `magnifying-lens` | A glass lens magnifies your chest, then opens out | | `portal` | A ring of blue light opens and the camera flies through it | | `clone-room` | Copies of you step out behind you | | `infinite-zoom` | A frame inside a frame, and the camera zooms through both | | `cube-spin` | Your shot turns a quarter on a 3D cube | | `liquid-glass` | A drop of glass grows into a pane and the camera dives through | | `screen-in-screen` | Pulls back to a laptop playing your shot, then dives back in | | `frame-break` | You lean out of a printed photo of yourself | | `tile-tunnel` | Flies backwards down a tunnel, then back into you | | `depth-ui` | App windows float at different depths around you | | `vertigo` | A dolly zoom down a gridded corridor | | `phone-fan` | Your shot on a phone, four more fan out behind it | | `shatter` | Your shot cracks like glass and the shards fly past | | `spotlight` | Lights down, one theatre light on your face | | `pull-back-reveal` | Pulls back to show your shot inside a video editor | | `ribbon-wrap` | A ribbon with your words wraps round you | | `zoom-through` | A chat with your ask, then a fly-through into your clip | | `head-pop-out` | Your head springs out of a blue panel. An ending | ## Rules every skill shares - The recording is the source of truth. Captions follow what was said. - One idea per beat. The scene changes every 3-5 seconds. - Every object fills its panel. Small things in big white space look cheap. - Captions sit in one pill at the same height on every beat, always on. - Size objects from `PANEL`, so every beat fits every size. - Real logos, real screenshots, real numbers. Never invent one. - Clone a style, never a brand. ## Licence MIT. Use it, change it, ship videos with it.

name: news-reaction
description: Edit a news or reaction video over real footage, one continuous run of footage per spoken line, played in source order, timed so the action lands on the word, with press headlines highlighted exactly on the ink and a music bed at one steady level. For industry news, market updates, commentary on a launch. Use when someone says "news video", "react to this launch", "put the footage behind me", "B-roll from the announcement", "footage edit" or has a real event clip to cover.
---

# News reaction video

**Use it for:** industry news, market updates, commentary on a launch.

For a real event with real footage. The footage tells the story, so the rules are about keeping it clean.

**Before you start:** run `video-intake` and `opening-hook` (look A, launch title, for news).

**Every size.** The same build makes 9:16, 4:5, 1:1 and 16:9. Size objects from `PANEL`, then run `every-format`.

## Step 1: Ask for three things, then wait

1. **The footage,** the original files you have the right to use. Note the source of each.
2. **The press shots,** if any: screenshots of real headlines.
3. **The cut transcript** with word timings.

## The rules that held up

- **One continuous run per spoken line.** Pick one stretch of one clip and play it straight. No hopping between moments of the same clip.
- **In source order.** Line 2's footage comes after line 1's in the original.
- **The action lands on the word.** "Let go" = the release. "Wheels" = the landing. Slide the run's start so the moment hits the word.
- **When the clip turns to something off topic** (a presenter, its own transition), hold its last useful frame instead.
- **Hard cuts between runs.** Static frame, no zooms, no effects. The footage is the effect.
- **Press headlines get a highlight on the ink,** never retyped. Trim the box to the letters, pad 3px.
- **Footage fills the top panel or the full frame.** Your face card or cut-out stays below it.

## Step 2: Build the shot list, then wait

One row per line: spoken words, start and end, clip file, the clip's in point, and the word the action lands on. Show it and wait for a yes.

## Step 3: Pull frames and build

```
ffmpeg -ss <in> -t <length> -i clip.mp4 -vf "fps=30,scale=1080:-2" -q:v 3 shots/03/%06d.jpg
```

Paste into Claude Code:

```
Edit video.js only. One beat per row of my shot list. Each beat shows shots/NN/ frames in order, frame = round((t - beat start) * 30) + 1, held on its last frame if the line runs longer.
Layout split: footage fills the top panel, my face card below. Hard cut between beats, no zoom, no transition.
Press shots: the screenshot fills the top panel, with one highlight box trimmed to the ink of [WORD], the rest greyed at rgba(255,255,255,.55).
Check a still at the landing word of every beat: the action must be on screen at that moment.
```

## Step 4: Music, then check

Run `video-sound` (one bed level to the last frame). Then `video-check`.

## What I learned the hard way

- **Cutting between three moments of one clip looks messy.** One clean run per line looks intentional.
- **A music take that fades early leaves the end of the video flat.** Cut it before its own fade and loop whole phrases.
- **Credit and rights matter more here than anywhere.** Use footage you are allowed to use.

name: brand-setup
description: Put your own brand into every video, read your website's real live stylesheets, write one design-system file (type, colour, shape, shadow, easing, durations), set the starter's colours, font and logo from it so every video comes out on brand, and turn it into a motion brief with 16 moments in that style. Works for any SaaS, app, agency or consumer brand, yours or a client's with permission. Use when someone says "use my brand", "brand my videos", "make motion graphics in my brand", "match my website", "brand design system for motion" or gives a website and wants videos that look like it.
---

# Brand setup: your brand in every video

Point it at your website. It reads the real styles the site ships, writes them down as one file, and sets every video in this pack to match. The same steps made my Apple and Stripe sets.

**Clone the style, never the brand.** The file holds values (fonts, colours, easing). Never logos, product shots, trademarks or copy. Clone a competitor's look for your own brand and you are copying, so use it on your own site, a client's with permission, or as a study.

## Step 1: Ask for two things, then wait

1. **The website,** one URL.
2. **Your logo,** an SVG or a PNG with a clear background.

## Step 2: Read the real styles

The live stylesheets are the truth. Screenshots and guesses are not.

```
Fetch [URL] and list every stylesheet it loads, including ones from its CDN. Download each one into styles/.
If a request is refused or filtered, tell me which domain, and stop so I can allow it. Do not guess the missing values.
```

A browser tool that saves a page's live stylesheets works too. I use REA (Reverse Engineer Anything), a free open-source tool. If the first run keeps only one file, read what it filtered out (often the brand's CDN domain), allow that domain, and run it again. That took me from 1 file to 94.

## Step 3: Write the design-system file

```
Read every file in styles/ and write [brand]-design-system.md with these sections, values only, each one counted from the CSS:
Type: font families, the weights actually used for body, headings and emphasis, letter-spacing on headings, any font-feature-settings.
Colour: background, surfaces, text, secondary text, the one accent and its pressed state, any gradient with its stops.
Shape: corner radii by size, the shadow tokens.
Motion: every transition and animation timing function, ranked by how often it is used, and the common durations.
Mark each value with how many times it appears. Say which fonts are paid and give a free fallback.
Never copy logos, images, product names or marketing copy into this file.
```

Read it. The top easing curve is the brand's feel: Stripe's fast snap was used 44 times, Apple's calm curve is symmetric.

## Step 4: Turn it into motion

```
Using [brand]-design-system.md as the house style, write a motion brief for [FORMAT] with 16 moments, each "thing → change" (for example "Checkout → paid", "0 → £12,480").
Every moment: ONE hero object filling 60-70% of the frame, ONE satisfying change, the brand's top easing curve and durations, hold the after state 1.2 seconds.
Use only values from the file. Never draw the brand's logo, wordmark or product screenshots.
```

Paste the brief into Claude Motion (claude.ai) or build it in Claude Code as one HTML file with `window.seek(seconds)`. See `apple-style` and `stripe-style` for two finished briefs made this way.

## Step 5: Put it into the starter

```
Open design-system.md. In index.html, set the :root values from it:
--bg (main background), --ink (main text), --accent (the one brand colour), --font (the brand font, loaded from its real source).
Copy the logo to logo.svg and show it 64px high in the top-left corner of the first and last beat only.
Then shoot stills at 1 and 5 seconds and show them to me next to a screenshot of the website.
```

From here on every skill in this pack draws in your brand. Run it once per brand.

## Check

- Does every value in the brief trace back to a line in the CSS?
- Is there no logo, wordmark or real screenshot anywhere?
- At 200px wide, does it still feel like the brand?

name: call-to-action
description: Build the right ending for each place a business posts a video, a comment-keyword ending for Instagram and TikTok (a clean comment box types the keyword, then the DM card with the link), a no-gate ending for LinkedIn with the links in the post, and a one-button end card for a website, a sales email or a YouTube end screen (book a call, start a trial, reply), all over the last 2-3 seconds, never extra seconds, plus the check that the delivery is live before posting. Use when someone says "call to action", "end card", "comment CTA", "comment to get", "book a call ending", "CTA for my video" or "ManyChat ending".
---

# Call to action

The ending decides what a view turns into. It sits over the last 2-3 seconds. It never adds extra seconds.

## Pick the ending by where the video goes

| Where | Ending | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Instagram, TikTok | **A. Comment keyword** (below) | A comment pushes the video and the DM delivers the link |
| LinkedIn | **B. No gate.** End on the payoff. Every link goes in the post text | A comment-for-the-link ask reads as bait there |
| Website, sales email, YouTube end screen, webinar page | **C. One-button end card** | The viewer is already warm. Give one clear next step |

One ending per file. When you render several sizes with `every-format`, give each one its own ending.

# A. Comment keyword

## Step 1: Ask for three things, then wait

1. **The keyword,** 4 or 5 letters, one word. Short words get typed. Long ones get skipped.
2. **What it sends,** in plain words ("the 16 skills", "the free guide").
3. **The delivery tool** (ManyChat or similar) and whether the flow is live yet.

## The look

- **A clean copy of the native Instagram comment box,** centred. Your avatar circle, "Add a comment…", the keyword typing in at about 8 characters a second.
- **Then the reply:** a DM bubble ("Here you go") and a link card under it, with clear space between the two.
- **It slides up into the last frame,** over the payoff. The payoff stays visible behind it.
- **Holds to the very last frame.**
- **Spoken line to match:** "Comment [KEYWORD] and I'll send you [the thing]."

## Step 2: Build brief (paste into Claude Code)

```
Over the last [2.5]s of video.js, add the comment CTA on top of the last beat. Do not cut away from the last beat.
A white comment sheet rises from the bottom to y 1060 (36px top corners, soft shadow): a 64px avatar circle, the field "Add a comment…" in grey 40px, then "[KEYWORD]" types in at 8 characters a second in #1d1d1f.
0.6s after the last letter, the field clears and a DM bubble "Here you go" (white, 28px corners) appears at y 760, then 0.3s later a link card "[WHAT IT SENDS]" with a 120px thumbnail under it, 40px gap between them.
Everything holds to the last frame. Nothing below y 1500 is text.
```

## Step 3: Before you post

- **The keyword flow is live and tested.** Comment the keyword yourself from another account and check the DM arrives.
- **The thing it sends exists** and matches what the video promised, word for word.
- **The caption repeats the keyword** in its first lines.

## What I learned the hard way

- **A custom-styled box looks cheap.** A faithful copy of the native comment UI looks premium.
- **Never add seconds for the CTA.** Put it over the ending.
- **An unsaved automation is a lost automation.** Duplicate a live flow, edit it, set it live, and read it back.

# C. One-button end card

## Ask for two things, then wait

1. **The action,** three words or fewer ("Book a call", "Start free", "Reply 'yes'").
2. **Where it goes,** the real URL or the reply address. Never a placeholder in a finished file.

## Build brief (paste into Claude Code)

```
Over the last [2.5]s of video.js, add an end card on top of the last beat. Do not cut away from the last beat.
A white card rises from the bottom (40px corners, soft long shadow), centred in the motion panel, PANEL.w * 0.7 wide.
Line 1, 56px, brand ink: the promise in five words or fewer ("Get this set up for you").
Line 2: one pill button in the brand accent with white text: "[ACTION]", and the URL under it in grey 32px.
The button settles with a small spring 0.3s after the card. It holds to the very last frame.
Spoken line to match: "[ACTION] at [short URL]."
```

## Check

- The URL is real and loads. Open it once.
- The button text matches the spoken line word for word.
- On a sales email, the thumbnail (frame 0) shows the person's name or company if the email is personal.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Validate every skill in skills/ against the Agent Skills spec.
# Checks: YAML frontmatter, required fields, name matches folder, description length,
# file size, standard folder structure, and the pack's house style: no em dashes or
# semicolons in prose (code blocks are skipped), no local /Users/ paths, no "steal".
# Also checks every skill's references/*.md and every prompts/*.md file for the same house style.

set -u

ROOT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
SKILLS_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/skills"
PROMPTS_DIR="$ROOT_DIR/prompts"
PASS=0
WARN=0
FAIL=0
SKILL_COUNT=0
PROMPT_COUNT=0

GREEN='\033[0;32m'
YELLOW='\033[0;33m'
RED='\033[0;31m'
CYAN='\033[0;36m'
NC='\033[0m'

err()  { printf "  ${RED}x${NC} %s\n" "$1"; FAIL=$((FAIL+1)); }
warn() { printf "  ${YELLOW}!${NC} %s\n" "$1"; WARN=$((WARN+1)); }
ok()   { printf "  ${GREEN}v${NC} %s\n" "$1"; PASS=$((PASS+1)); }

# House style for any markdown file: prose outside fenced code blocks, inline code stripped.
check_style() {
  local file="$1" label="$2" prose
  prose="$(awk '/^```/{f=!f; next} !f' "$file")"
  if printf "%s" "$prose" | grep -q $'\xe2\x80\x94'; then
    err "$label: em dash found in prose"
  else
    ok "$label: no em dashes in prose"
  fi
  if printf "%s" "$prose" | sed 's/`[^`]*`//g' | grep -q ';'; then
    err "$label: semicolon found in prose"
  else
    ok "$label: no semicolons in prose"
  fi
  if grep -q '/Users/' "$file"; then
    err "$label: local /Users/ path found"
  else
    ok "$label: no local paths"
  fi
  if grep -qiw 'steal' "$file"; then
    err "$label: banned word 'steal' found"
  fi
}

printf "${CYAN}Validating skills in %s${NC}\n\n" "$SKILLS_DIR"

if [[ ! -d "$SKILLS_DIR" ]]; then
  printf "${RED}skills/ folder not found.${NC}\n"
  exit 1
fi

for skill_dir in "$SKILLS_DIR"/*/; do
  [[ -d "$skill_dir" ]] || continue
  SKILL_COUNT=$((SKILL_COUNT+1))
  skill_name="$(basename "$skill_dir")"
  skill_md="${skill_dir}SKILL.md"

  printf "${CYAN}%s${NC}\n" "$skill_name"

  # SKILL.md exists
  if [[ ! -f "$skill_md" ]]; then
    err "SKILL.md missing"
    continue
  fi

  # Folder name format
  if [[ ! "$skill_name" =~ ^[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*$ ]]; then
    err "folder name must be lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens"
  else
    ok "folder name valid"
  fi

  # Frontmatter present
  first_line="$(head -n1 "$skill_md")"
  if [[ "$first_line" != "---" ]]; then
    err "SKILL.md must start with YAML frontmatter (---)"
    continue
  fi

  # Extract frontmatter (between the first two --- delimiters)
  frontmatter="$(awk '/^---[[:space:]]*$/{n++; next} n==1{print} n==2{exit}' "$skill_md")"

  # Frontmatter must parse as YAML, or skill installers drop the skill silently
  yaml_err="$(printf "%s\n" "$frontmatter" | python3 -c 'import sys
try:
    import yaml
except ImportError:
    print("SKIP"); sys.exit(0)
try:
    d = yaml.safe_load(sys.stdin.read())
    assert isinstance(d, dict), "frontmatter is not a mapping"
except Exception as e:
    print(str(e).splitlines()[0])' 2>&1)"
  if [[ "$yaml_err" == "SKIP" ]]; then
    warn "PyYAML not installed, YAML parse not checked"
  elif [[ -n "$yaml_err" ]]; then
    err "frontmatter is not valid YAML: $yaml_err"
  else
    ok "frontmatter parses as YAML"
  fi

  # name field
  yaml_name="$(printf "%s" "$frontmatter" | awk -F': ' '/^name:/{print $2; exit}' | tr -d '"' | tr -d "'" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
  if [[ -z "$yaml_name" ]]; then
    err "name field missing from frontmatter"
  elif [[ "$yaml_name" != "$skill_name" ]]; then
    err "name '$yaml_name' does not match folder '$skill_name'"
  else
    ok "name matches folder"
  fi

  if [[ ${#yaml_name} -gt 64 ]]; then
    err "name exceeds 64 characters"
  fi

  # description field — parse only the frontmatter we already extracted (not the body)
  desc_block="$(printf "%s\n" "$frontmatter" | awk '
    BEGIN{in_desc=0}
    /^description:/{
      sub(/^description:[ \t]*/, "")
      if ($0 ~ /^>/ || $0 ~ /^\|/) { in_desc=1; next }
      print; exit
    }
    in_desc==1 {
      if ($0 ~ /^[a-zA-Z_-]+:/) exit
      sub(/^[ \t]+/, "")
      printf "%s ", $0
    }
  ')"

  desc_len=${#desc_block}
  if [[ $desc_len -eq 0 ]]; then
    err "description field missing or empty"
  elif [[ $desc_len -gt 1024 ]]; then
    err "description is $desc_len chars, must be 1024 or fewer"
  else
    ok "description present ($desc_len chars)"
  fi

  # Trigger phrase hint
  if [[ "$desc_block" == *"when"* || "$desc_block" == *"Use"* || "$desc_block" == *"use"* ]]; then
    ok "description has trigger phrasing"
  else
    warn "description should include 'use' or 'when' trigger phrasing"
  fi

  # File size
  line_count=$(wc -l < "$skill_md" | tr -d '[:space:]')
  if [[ $line_count -gt 500 ]]; then
    warn "SKILL.md is $line_count lines, consider moving detail to references/"
  else
    ok "SKILL.md size OK ($line_count lines)"
  fi

  # House style: prose outside fenced code blocks
  prose="$(awk '/^```/{f=!f; next} !f' "$skill_md")"
  if printf "%s" "$prose" | grep -q $'\xe2\x80\x94'; then
    err "em dash found in prose"
  else
    ok "no em dashes in prose"
  fi
  if printf "%s" "$prose" | sed 's/`[^`]*`//g' | grep -q ';'; then
    err "semicolon found in prose"
  else
    ok "no semicolons in prose"
  fi
  if grep -rq '/Users/' "$skill_dir"; then
    err "local /Users/ path found"
  else
    ok "no local paths"
  fi
  if grep -rqiw 'steal' "$skill_dir"; then
    err "banned word 'steal' found"
  fi

  # House style in reference files
  if [[ -d "${skill_dir}references" ]]; then
    for ref in "${skill_dir}references"/*.md; do
      [[ -f "$ref" ]] || continue
      check_style "$ref" "references/$(basename "$ref")"
    done
  fi

  # Optional standard folders
  for sub in references scripts assets; do
    if [[ -d "${skill_dir}${sub}" ]]; then
      ok "has ${sub}/ folder"
    fi
  done

  printf "\n"
done

if [[ -d "$PROMPTS_DIR" ]]; then
  printf "${CYAN}prompts${NC}\n"
  for prompt_md in "$PROMPTS_DIR"/*.md; do
    [[ -f "$prompt_md" ]] || continue
    PROMPT_COUNT=$((PROMPT_COUNT+1))
    check_style "$prompt_md" "$(basename "$prompt_md")"
    # Every fenced block must be closed
    fences=$(grep -c '^```' "$prompt_md")
    if (( fences % 2 != 0 )); then
      err "$(basename "$prompt_md"): unclosed code block"
    fi
  done
  printf "\n"
fi

printf "${CYAN}Summary${NC}\n"
printf "  Skills checked: %d\n" "$SKILL_COUNT"
printf "  Prompt files checked: %d\n" "$PROMPT_COUNT"
printf "  ${GREEN}Passed:${NC}   %d\n" "$PASS"
printf "  ${YELLOW}Warnings:${NC} %d\n" "$WARN"
printf "  ${RED}Failed:${NC}   %d\n" "$FAIL"

if [[ $FAIL -gt 0 ]]; then
  exit 1
fi
exit 0

{
  "name": "reel-editing-skills",
  "description": "Edit to-camera motion videos for any business with Claude Code. One build, every platform. 21 editing skills plus 20 one-command effects.",

  "author": { "name": "Charlie Hills" },
  "license": "MIT"
}

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Cut ranked clips from a long recording, with a two-line hook and word-by-word captions.
usage: python3 make-clips.py long.mp4 audio.json clips.json [--ink 1d1d1f] [--accent 0071e3] [--bg ffffff] [--font "Helvetica Neue"]
writes clip<rank>.ass and clips/clip<rank>.mp4 (1080 x 1920, H.264, limited range)."""
import json, re, subprocess, sys, os, argparse

p = argparse.ArgumentParser()
p.add_argument('src'); p.add_argument('words'); p.add_argument('clips')
p.add_argument('--ink', default='1d1d1f'); p.add_argument('--accent', default='0071e3')
p.add_argument('--bg', default='ffffff'); p.add_argument('--font', default='Helvetica Neue')
a = p.parse_args()

def bgr(h): return f"&H00{h[4:6]}{h[2:4]}{h[0:2]}".upper()
INK, ACC = bgr(a.ink), bgr(a.accent)
def ts(t):
    t = max(0, t); return f"{int(t // 3600)}:{int(t % 3600 // 60):02d}:{t % 60:05.2f}"

W = [(w['start'], w['end'], w['word'].strip()) for s in json.load(open(a.words))['segments'] for w in s['words']]
w0, h0 = map(int, subprocess.check_output(['ffprobe', '-v', 'error', '-select_streams', 'v:0', '-show_entries',
          'stream=width,height', '-of', 'csv=p=0', a.src]).decode().split(',')[:2])
vertical = h0 > w0
# landscape: source band across the middle. vertical: source full frame
band_h = 1920 if vertical else round(1080 * h0 / w0 / 2) * 2
band_y = 0 if vertical else 660
hook_v, cap_v = (220, 900) if vertical else (330, band_y + band_h + 80)

os.makedirs('clips', exist_ok=True)
for c in json.load(open(a.clips)):
    s, e, r = c['start'], c['end'], c['rank']
    words = [w for w in W if w[0] >= s - 0.01 and w[1] <= e + 0.01]
    chunks, cur = [], []
    for i, w in enumerate(words):
        cur.append(w); nxt = words[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(words) else None
        if len(cur) == 3 or re.search(r'[.,?!]$', w[2]) or not nxt or nxt[0] - w[1] > 0.3:
            chunks.append(cur); cur = []
    box = 3 if vertical else 1   # a solid pill behind captions over a full-frame face
    head = f"""[Script Info]
ScriptType: v4.00+
PlayResX: 1080
PlayResY: 1920
WrapStyle: 2

[V4+ Styles]
Format: Name, Fontname, Fontsize, PrimaryColour, SecondaryColour, OutlineColour, BackColour, Bold, Italic, Underline, StrikeOut, ScaleX, ScaleY, Spacing, Angle, BorderStyle, Outline, Shadow, Alignment, MarginL, MarginR, MarginV, Encoding
Style: Hook,{a.font},80,{INK},{INK},&H00FFFFFF,&H00FFFFFF,-1,0,0,0,100,100,-1,0,{box},18,0,8,70,70,{hook_v},1
Style: Cap,{a.font},64,{INK},{INK},&H00FFFFFF,&H00FFFFFF,-1,0,0,0,100,100,0,0,{box},14,0,8,70,70,{cap_v},1

[Events]
Format: Layer, Start, End, Style, Name, MarginL, MarginR, MarginV, Effect, Text
"""
    ev = [f"Dialogue: 0,{ts(0)},{ts(e - s)},Hook,,0,0,0,,{c['hook']}"]
    for ch in chunks:
        for j, w in enumerate(ch):
            st = (ch[0][0] if j == 0 else w[0]) - s
            en = (ch[j + 1][0] if j + 1 < len(ch) else ch[-1][1] + 0.15) - s
            txt = ' '.join((f"{{\\c{ACC}&}}{x[2]}{{\\c{INK}&}}" if k == j else x[2]) for k, x in enumerate(ch))
            ev.append(f"Dialogue: 1,{ts(st)},{ts(en)},Cap,,0,0,0,,{txt}")
    open(f'clip{r}.ass', 'w').write(head + '\n'.join(ev) + '\n')
    d = e - s
    fit = 'scale=1080:1920:force_original_aspect_ratio=increase,crop=1080:1920' if vertical else f'scale=1080:{band_h}:flags=lanczos'
    fc = (f"[0:v]{fit},setsar=1[v];[1:v][v]overlay=0:{band_y}:shortest=1,ass=clip{r}.ass,"
          f"scale=out_range=limited,format=yuv420p[o];"
          f"[0:a]afade=t=in:d=0.03,afade=t=out:st={d - 0.03:.2f}:d=0.03[a]")
    subprocess.run(['ffmpeg', '-v', 'error', '-y', '-ss', f'{s:.2f}', '-t', f'{d:.2f}', '-i', a.src,
                    '-f', 'lavfi', '-i', f'color=0x{a.bg}:s=1080x1920:r=30', '-filter_complex', fc,
                    '-map', '[o]', '-map', '[a]', '-c:v', 'libx264', '-profile:v', 'high', '-crf', '19',
                    '-color_range', 'tv', '-colorspace', 'bt709', '-color_primaries', 'bt709', '-color_trc', 'bt709',
                    '-c:a', 'aac', '-b:a', '160k', '-ar', '44100', '-movflags', '+faststart', f'clips/clip{r}.mp4'], check=True)
    print(f"clips/clip{r}.mp4  {d:.1f}s  {c['hook'].replace(chr(92) + 'N', ' / ')}")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Get your clip ready for an effect. run.cjs calls this for you, in two passes.

  python3 prep.py frames <clip> <work> [--from S] [--to S] [--no-fit]
      Finds your head in 5 sample frames, scales and crops the clip to 1080x1920 so your head sits where the effects
      expect it, and writes every frame at 30fps to <work>/p/NNNNN.jpg. Prints one JSON line: frame count and the fit.
  python3 prep.py matte <work> <need.json>
      Cuts you out (RobustVideoMatting) on the frames the effect needs: <work>/c/NNNNN.png.
      Writes the stills it asks for to <work>/stills/: plate<label>.jpg, cut<label>.png and 324px thumbnails (<label>s).

Needs ffmpeg, Python 3 with torch, torchvision, pillow and numpy. torch.hub downloads the matting model once
(RobustVideoMatting, GPL-3.0, not bundled here). Runs on Apple Silicon (mps), NVIDIA (cuda) or the CPU (slow).
"""
import argparse, json, os, subprocess, sys, tempfile
import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

W, H, FPS = 1080, 1920, 30
# The head every effect is drawn around, measured with head() below on the 24 cut-outs the effects were built on (1080x1920):
# median crown row 415 and head width 502px. Your head is centred (x 540), where the effects' face box sits.
REF = {'crown': 415, 'width': 502, 'cx': 540}


def head(alpha):
    """Crown row, head width and head centre x of a person matte (uint8 HxW). None if no person is found."""
    m = alpha > 128
    rows = m.sum(1)
    ys = np.nonzero(rows > 20)[0]
    if not len(ys):
        return None
    crown = int(ys[0])
    c = float(np.nonzero(m[crown])[0].mean())
    best, cx = 0, None
    for y in range(crown, min(m.shape[0], crown + 900)):
        row = m[y]
        ci = int(round(c))
        if not row[ci]:   # the run under the centre line, or the nearest one
            xs = np.nonzero(row)[0]
            if not len(xs):
                continue
            ci = int(xs[np.argmin(np.abs(xs - c))])
        x0 = ci - (np.argmin(row[ci::-1]) if not row[ci::-1].all() else ci + 1) + 1
        x1 = ci + (np.argmin(row[ci:]) if not row[ci:].all() else len(row) - ci) - 1
        w = int(x1 - x0 + 1)
        # the head ends at the neck (the outline narrows below 0.8x the widest row so far), or where the shoulders
        # widen past 1.3x it (long hair, no visible neck)
        if y - crown > 120 and best and (w < .8 * best or w > 1.3 * best):
            break
        if w > best:
            best, cx = w, (x0 + x1) / 2
        if y - crown < 200:
            c = (x0 + x1) / 2   # follow the head while it is still the top of the outline
    if not best:
        return None
    return {'crown': crown, 'width': best, 'cx': float(cx)}


def fill_holes(a):
    """Fill holes in the matte that do not touch the top or sides (a mic or a hand in front of the body)."""
    sm = Image.fromarray(np.where(a < 100, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).resize((270, 480), Image.NEAREST)
    w, h = sm.size
    px = sm.load()
    for x, y in [(x, 0) for x in range(0, w, 5)] + [(0, y) for y in range(0, h, 5)] + [(w - 1, y) for y in range(0, h, 5)]:
        if px[x, y] == 0:
            ImageDraw.floodfill(sm, (x, y), 128)
    a = a.copy()
    a[np.asarray(sm.resize((a.shape[1], a.shape[0]), Image.NEAREST)) == 0] = 255
    return a


class Matte:
    def __init__(self):
        import torch
        self.torch = torch
        self.dev = 'mps' if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else ('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')
        self.m = torch.hub.load('PeterL1n/RobustVideoMatting', 'resnet50', trust_repo=True).eval().to(self.dev)
        self.rec, self.last = [None] * 4, -9

    def __call__(self, im, k=None, settle=False):
        """im: HxWx3 uint8. k: frame number (a run of k, k+1, ... keeps the model's memory). Returns alpha uint8."""
        t = self.torch
        with t.no_grad():
            x = t.from_numpy(im.copy()).to(self.dev).permute(2, 0, 1).unsqueeze(0).float() / 255
            ds = min(.25, 512 / max(im.shape[:2]))
            if settle or k is None or k != self.last + 1:
                self.rec = [None] * 4
                for _ in range(3):
                    _, _, *self.rec = self.m(x, *self.rec, downsample_ratio=ds)
            self.last = k if k is not None else -9
            _, pha, *self.rec = self.m(x, *self.rec, downsample_ratio=ds)
            return (pha[0, 0].clamp(0, 1).cpu().numpy() * 255).astype(np.uint8)


def ff(*a):
    subprocess.run(['ffmpeg', '-v', 'error', '-y', *a], check=True)


def frames(a):
    clip, work = a.clip, a.work
    os.makedirs(work + '/p', exist_ok=True)
    trim = (['-ss', str(a.t0)] if a.t0 else []) + (['-to', str(a.t1)] if a.t1 is not None else [])
    dur = float(subprocess.run(['ffprobe', '-v', 'error', '-show_entries', 'format=duration', '-of', 'csv=p=0', clip],
                               capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout.strip())
    t0, t1 = a.t0 or 0, (a.t1 if a.t1 is not None else dur)
    # the clip at height 1920, its own shape (a landscape clip stays wide here)
    tmp = tempfile.mkdtemp(dir=work)
    for i in range(5):
        ts = t0 + (t1 - t0) * (i + .5) / 5
        ff('-ss', f'{ts:.3f}', '-i', clip, '-frames:v', '1', '-vf', f'scale=-2:{H}:flags=lanczos', f'{tmp}/s{i}.png')
    samples = [np.asarray(Image.open(f'{tmp}/s{i}.png').convert('RGB')) for i in range(5)]
    nw = samples[0].shape[1]
    fit = {'scale': max(1.0, W / nw), 'x': None, 'y': 0, 'found': 0, 'note': ''}
    if not a.no_fit:
        mat = Matte()
        hs = [h for h in (head(mat(s, settle=True)) for s in samples) if h]
        fit['found'] = len(hs)
        if hs:
            med = {k: float(np.median([h[k] for h in hs])) for k in REF}
            k = REF['width'] / med['width']
            cover = max(1.0, W / nw)
            if k < cover:
                fit['note'] += f'You fill more of the frame than the effects expect, so you show {cover / k:.2f}x bigger than the reference. '
            if k > 2.5:
                fit['note'] += 'You are small in the frame, so the zoom is capped at 2.5x and you sit smaller than the effects expect. '
            k = min(2.5, max(cover, k))
            x = med['cx'] * k - REF['cx']
            y = med['crown'] * k - REF['crown']
            sw, sh = nw * k, H * k
            xc, yc = min(max(0, x), sw - W), min(max(0, y), sh - H)
            if yc - y > 40:
                fit['note'] += f'There is little room above your head, so it sits {yc - y:.0f}px higher than the effects expect. '
            if y - yc > 40:
                fit['note'] += f'Your head is low in the frame, so it sits {y - yc:.0f}px lower than the effects expect. '
            if abs(xc - x) > 40:
                fit['note'] += f'You are near the edge of the frame, so you sit {abs(xc - x):.0f}px off centre. '
            fit.update(scale=round(k, 4), x=round(xc), y=round(yc), head=med)
        else:
            fit['note'] = 'No person found in the sample frames, so the clip is centred as it is. '
    for f in os.listdir(tmp):
        os.remove(os.path.join(tmp, f))
    os.rmdir(tmp)
    k = fit['scale']
    sw, sh = int(round(nw * k / 2) * 2), int(round(H * k / 2) * 2)
    x = fit['x'] if fit['x'] is not None else (sw - W) // 2
    x, y = int(min(max(0, x), sw - W)), int(min(max(0, fit['y']), sh - H))
    ff(*trim, '-i', clip, '-vf', f'fps={FPS},scale={sw}:{sh}:flags=lanczos:out_range=pc,crop={W}:{H}:{x}:{y},format=yuvj420p',
       '-q:v', '2', '-start_number', '0', f'{work}/p/%05d.jpg')
    n = len([f for f in os.listdir(work + '/p') if f.endswith('.jpg')])
    fit.update(x=x, y=y)
    print(json.dumps({'frames': n, 'fit': fit}))


def matte(a):
    work = a.work
    need = json.load(open(a.need))
    os.makedirs(work + '/c', exist_ok=True)
    os.makedirs(work + '/stills', exist_ok=True)
    n = len([f for f in os.listdir(work + '/p') if f.endswith('.jpg')])
    mat = Matte()
    frames_ = sorted(set(min(n - 1, int(k)) for k in need['c']))
    for i, k in enumerate(frames_):
        im = np.asarray(Image.open('%s/p/%05d.jpg' % (work, k)).convert('RGB'))
        al = fill_holes(mat(im, k))
        Image.fromarray(np.dstack([im, al]), 'RGBA').save('%s/c/%05d.png' % (work, k), compress_level=1)
        if i % 50 == 0:
            print('matte', i, len(frames_), flush=True)
    # stills: 'e' = 0.3s into the effect, 'k1'..'k19' = moments spread across the clip
    for lab, kinds in need['stills'].items():
        if lab == 'e':
            k = round((need['at'] + .3) * FPS)
        else:
            j = int(lab[1:])
            k = round((j % 20) / 20 * (n - 1))
        k = min(n - 1, max(0, k))
        im = Image.open('%s/p/%05d.jpg' % (work, k)).convert('RGB')
        for kind in kinds:
            if kind == 'plate':
                im.save(f'{work}/stills/plate{lab}.jpg', quality=92)
                im.resize((324, 576), Image.LANCZOS).save(f'{work}/stills/plate{lab}s.jpg', quality=90)
            else:
                ar = np.asarray(im)
                al = fill_holes(mat(ar, settle=True))
                c = Image.fromarray(np.dstack([ar, al]), 'RGBA')
                c.save(f'{work}/stills/cut{lab}.png', compress_level=1)
                c.resize((324, 576), Image.LANCZOS).save(f'{work}/stills/cut{lab}s.png')
    print('matte done', len(frames_), 'frames,', len(need['stills']), 'stills', flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split('\n')[0])
    sub = ap.add_subparsers(dest='cmd', required=True)
    f = sub.add_parser('frames')
    f.add_argument('clip')
    f.add_argument('work')
    f.add_argument('--from', dest='t0', type=float, default=0)
    f.add_argument('--to', dest='t1', type=float, default=None)
    f.add_argument('--no-fit', action='store_true', help='keep your framing, only scale and centre-crop to 1080x1920')
    m = sub.add_parser('matte')
    m.add_argument('work')
    m.add_argument('need')
    a = ap.parse_args()
    frames(a) if a.cmd == 'frames' else matte(a)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Optional depth step: the room without you in it (a clean plate).

Reads  <video>/face/NNNNNN.jpg and <video>/cut/NNNNNN.webp (run matte.py first, same range)
Writes <video>/plate.jpg

The template blurs this plate behind the page and pushes the camera in slowly.
Your blurred ghost never shows, because you are not in the plate.
Only for a camera on a tripod. A handheld shot moves, so the plate will not line up.

  python3 plate.py my-video --from 12.4 --to 17.0
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys
import warnings

import numpy as np
from PIL import Image, ImageFilter

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
ap.add_argument('video')
ap.add_argument('--from', dest='t0', type=float, default=0.0)
ap.add_argument('--to', dest='t1', type=float, required=True)
ap.add_argument('--fps', type=float, default=30.0)
a = ap.parse_args()

n0, n1 = round(a.t0 * a.fps) + 1, round(a.t1 * a.fps) + 1
S = (540, 960)  # work at half size, then scale up. The plate is blurred anyway
acc, msk = [], []
for n in range(n0, n1 + 1, 3):
    cut = None
    for ext in ('webp', 'png'):
        p = os.path.join(a.video, 'cut', f'{n:06d}.{ext}')
        if os.path.exists(p):
            cut = p
            break
    face = os.path.join(a.video, 'face', f'{n:06d}.jpg')
    if not cut or not os.path.exists(face):
        continue
    al = np.asarray(Image.open(cut).resize(S, Image.BILINEAR).getchannel('A').filter(ImageFilter.MaxFilter(7)), np.float32) / 255
    acc.append(np.asarray(Image.open(face).convert('RGB').resize(S, Image.BILINEAR), np.float32))
    msk.append(al < .04)
if not acc:
    sys.exit('No frame pairs found. Run matte.py on the same range first.')

acc, msk = np.stack(acc), np.stack(msk)
# per pixel: the median colour over the frames where you are not covering it
with warnings.catch_warnings():
    warnings.simplefilter('ignore', RuntimeWarning)  # pixels you always cover are all-NaN. They are filled below
    plate = np.nan_to_num(np.nanmedian(np.where(msk[..., None], acc, np.nan), axis=0))
known = msk.sum(0) >= 2


def box(x, r, ax):
    p = np.pad(x, [(r + 1, r) if i == ax else (0, 0) for i in range(x.ndim)], mode='edge')
    c = np.cumsum(p, axis=ax, dtype=np.float64)
    hi = np.take(c, range(2 * r + 1, c.shape[ax]), axis=ax)
    lo = np.take(c, range(0, c.shape[ax] - 2 * r - 1), axis=ax)
    return ((hi - lo) / (2 * r + 1)).astype(np.float32)


def blur(x, r):
    r = max(1, int(r * .6))
    for _ in range(3):
        x = box(box(x, r, 0), r, 1)
    return x


# the pixels you always cover: fill them from the room around them, growing the radius
for r in (8, 24, 60, 140, 320):
    w = known.astype(np.float32)
    den = blur(w, r) + 1e-6
    fill = np.stack([blur(plate[..., c] * w, r) / den for c in range(3)], -1)
    upd = (~known) & (den > .02)
    plate[upd] = fill[upd]
    known |= upd

out = os.path.join(a.video, 'plate.jpg')
Image.fromarray(np.clip(plate, 0, 255).astype(np.uint8)).resize((1080, 1920), Image.BICUBIC).save(out, quality=93)
print('plate:', out, '| pixels never seen:', int((~known).sum()))

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Cut you out of your video, frame by frame.

Reads  <video>/face/NNNNNN.jpg   (the frames video-intake writes)
Writes <video>/cut/NNNNNN.webp   the same frame, background transparent, same numbers
Prints the top of your head in frame pixels. The templates take it as headTop.

  pip install torch torchvision pillow numpy     (once. scipy is optional, it fills small holes)
  python3 matte.py my-video --from 12.4 --to 17.0

Only matte the beats that need it. A full video of cut-outs takes a lot of disk.
Model: RobustVideoMatting, free, runs on your machine. torch.hub downloads it once from GitHub.
Runs on Apple Silicon (mps), an NVIDIA card (cuda) or the CPU (slow, but it works).
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

import numpy as np
import torch
from PIL import Image

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Cut the speaker out of face/ frames into cut/')
ap.add_argument('video', help='the video folder from video-intake (holds face/)')
ap.add_argument('--from', dest='t0', type=float, default=0.0, help='beat start, seconds in the cut')
ap.add_argument('--to', dest='t1', type=float, default=None, help='beat end, seconds in the cut')
ap.add_argument('--fps', type=float, default=30.0)
ap.add_argument('--model', default='resnet50', choices=['resnet50', 'mobilenetv3'],
                help='resnet50 = cleaner hair, mobilenetv3 = about 3x faster')
ap.add_argument('--png', action='store_true', help='write PNG instead of WebP (about 10x the disk)')
a = ap.parse_args()

face = os.path.join(a.video, 'face')
out = os.path.join(a.video, 'cut')
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
count = len([f for f in os.listdir(face) if f.endswith('.jpg')]) if os.path.isdir(face) else 0
if not count:
    sys.exit(f'No frames in {face}. Run video-intake first.')

# same frame number rule as the starter: frame = round(t * fps) + 1
n0 = max(1, round(a.t0 * a.fps) + 1)
n1 = count if a.t1 is None else min(count, round(a.t1 * a.fps) + 2)
warm = max(1, n0 - 15)  # the model remembers past frames, so start a little early and throw those away

dev = 'mps' if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else ('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')
model = torch.hub.load('PeterL1n/RobustVideoMatting', a.model, trust_repo=True).eval().to(dev)

try:
    from scipy import ndimage
except ImportError:
    ndimage = None

rec = [None] * 4
tops = []
ext = 'png' if a.png else 'webp'
with torch.no_grad():
    for n in range(warm, n1 + 1):
        path = os.path.join(face, f'{n:06d}.jpg')
        im = np.asarray(Image.open(path).convert('RGB'))
        x = torch.from_numpy(im.copy()).to(dev).permute(2, 0, 1).unsqueeze(0).float() / 255
        fgr, pha, *rec = model(x, *rec, downsample_ratio=0.25)
        if n < n0:
            continue
        al = (pha[0, 0].clamp(0, 1).cpu().numpy() * 255).astype(np.uint8)
        solid = al > 128
        if ndimage is not None:
            # fill small holes inside you (a mic, a dark shirt) but never a real gap, like the space between arm and body
            holes = ndimage.binary_fill_holes(solid) & ~solid
            lab, k = ndimage.label(holes)
            if k:
                sizes = ndimage.sum(holes, lab, range(1, k + 1))
                small = np.isin(lab, 1 + np.flatnonzero(sizes < 2500))
                al[small] = 255
        rows = np.flatnonzero(solid.sum(1) > 30)
        if len(rows):
            tops.append(int(rows[0]))
        rgba = Image.fromarray(np.dstack([im, al]))
        dst = os.path.join(out, f'{n:06d}.{ext}')
        if a.png:
            rgba.save(dst, compress_level=3)
        else:
            rgba.save(dst, 'WEBP', quality=92, alpha_quality=100, method=4)
        if (n - n0) % 30 == 0:
            print(f'  frame {n}/{n1}', flush=True)

print(f'cut-outs: {out}/{n0:06d}.{ext} to {n1:06d}.{ext}')
if tops:
    print(f'headTop: {int(np.median(tops))}   (highest {min(tops)}, lowest {max(tops)}, frame pixels)')
else:
    print('headTop: none found. Is the person in these frames?')

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Cut you out of your video, frame by frame.

Reads  <video>/face/NNNNNN.jpg   (the frames video-intake writes)
Writes <video>/cut/NNNNNN.webp   the same frame, background transparent, same numbers
Prints the top of your head in frame pixels. The templates take it as headTop.

  pip install torch torchvision pillow numpy     (once. scipy is optional, it fills small holes)
  python3 matte.py my-video --from 12.4 --to 17.0

Only matte the beats that need it. A full video of cut-outs takes a lot of disk.
Model: RobustVideoMatting, free, runs on your machine. torch.hub downloads it once from GitHub.
Runs on Apple Silicon (mps), an NVIDIA card (cuda) or the CPU (slow, but it works).
"""
import argparse
import os
import sys

import numpy as np
import torch
from PIL import Image

ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description='Cut the speaker out of face/ frames into cut/')
ap.add_argument('video', help='the video folder from video-intake (holds face/)')
ap.add_argument('--from', dest='t0', type=float, default=0.0, help='beat start, seconds in the cut')
ap.add_argument('--to', dest='t1', type=float, default=None, help='beat end, seconds in the cut')
ap.add_argument('--fps', type=float, default=30.0)
ap.add_argument('--model', default='resnet50', choices=['resnet50', 'mobilenetv3'],
                help='resnet50 = cleaner hair, mobilenetv3 = about 3x faster')
ap.add_argument('--png', action='store_true', help='write PNG instead of WebP (about 10x the disk)')
a = ap.parse_args()

face = os.path.join(a.video, 'face')
out = os.path.join(a.video, 'cut')
os.makedirs(out, exist_ok=True)
count = len([f for f in os.listdir(face) if f.endswith('.jpg')]) if os.path.isdir(face) else 0
if not count:
    sys.exit(f'No frames in {face}. Run video-intake first.')

# same frame number rule as the starter: frame = round(t * fps) + 1
n0 = max(1, round(a.t0 * a.fps) + 1)
n1 = count if a.t1 is None else min(count, round(a.t1 * a.fps) + 2)
warm = max(1, n0 - 15)  # the model remembers past frames, so start a little early and throw those away

dev = 'mps' if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else ('cuda' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')
model = torch.hub.load('PeterL1n/RobustVideoMatting', a.model, trust_repo=True).eval().to(dev)

try:
    from scipy import ndimage
except ImportError:
    ndimage = None

rec = [None] * 4
tops = []
ext = 'png' if a.png else 'webp'
with torch.no_grad():
    for n in range(warm, n1 + 1):
        path = os.path.join(face, f'{n:06d}.jpg')
        im = np.asarray(Image.open(path).convert('RGB'))
        x = torch.from_numpy(im.copy()).to(dev).permute(2, 0, 1).unsqueeze(0).float() / 255
        fgr, pha, *rec = model(x, *rec, downsample_ratio=0.25)
        if n < n0:
            continue
        al = (pha[0, 0].clamp(0, 1).cpu().numpy() * 255).astype(np.uint8)
        solid = al > 128
        if ndimage is not None:
            # fill small holes inside you (a mic, a dark shirt) but never a real gap, like the space between arm and body
            holes = ndimage.binary_fill_holes(solid) & ~solid
            lab, k = ndimage.label(holes)
            if k:
                sizes = ndimage.sum(holes, lab, range(1, k + 1))
                small = np.isin(lab, 1 + np.flatnonzero(sizes < 2500))
                al[small] = 255
        rows = np.flatnonzero(solid.sum(1) > 30)
        if len(rows):
            tops.append(int(rows[0]))
        rgba = Image.fromarray(np.dstack([im, al]))
        dst = os.path.join(out, f'{n:06d}.{ext}')
        if a.png:
            rgba.save(dst, compress_level=3)
        else:
            rgba.save(dst, 'WEBP', quality=92, alpha_quality=100, method=4)
        if (n - n0) % 30 == 0:
            print(f'  frame {n}/{n1}', flush=True)

print(f'cut-outs: {out}/{n0:06d}.{ext} to {n1:06d}.{ext}')
if tops:
    print(f'headTop: {int(np.median(tops))}   (highest {min(tops)}, lowest {max(tops)}, frame pixels)')
else:
    print('headTop: none found. Is the person in these frames?')
